title: Boxing lessons and never playing prize fights
summary: He never played prize fights but loved boxing; a teacher taught him self-defense and would not let him fight professionally.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you ever play any prize fights? No. Never played prize fights. I heard guys talk about that, like Johnny Law and Tony Sparbo and different guys talk about going and playing prize fights between the rounds. Yeah. But I never saw that.
No, I never threw around with that at all.

Yes, I liked it so much that I wanted to do it myself. Oh, you wanted to do it? Yes, sir. I started out there and I had pretty good teachers and so forth. The old man told me one day, he says, he said, I'm on a table and eat and he says, how do you like boxing? I just come in. I said, I like it all right, here I'm boxing. He says, I'm going to tell you. He says, you got there and learn all you can learn for self-defense. But today you have to accept the nickel fight. He said, I'm going to get off. He would not let me get in and save his life.
I guess he was afraid you might get punchy or something. Fighting too much, too tough a game.
No, the only way he was peculiar about that fight, didn't he? He was very peculiar about that. That was good self-defense. Learn all you can.
